name: Plank
instructions: Set your forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.
Extend your legs back and rise onto your toes.
Form one straight line from heels to head.
Hold, breathing steadily. Reps are counted in seconds.
keyCues: Squeeze your glutes and tuck your ribs down.
Push the floor away to spread your shoulder blades.
Stop the set when the hips start to sag.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
Piking the hips up to make it easier.
Holding the breath through the set.

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on one side with your elbow under your shoulder.
Stack your feet and lift your hips off the floor.
Form a straight line from ankles to head.
Hold, then switch sides. Reps are counted in seconds.
keyCues: Push your bottom hip up toward the ceiling.
Keep your top shoulder stacked over the bottom one.
Bend the bottom knee to make it easier.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drift toward the floor.
Rolling the chest forward out of alignment.
Placing the elbow too far ahead of the shoulder.

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on your back with arms straight up and knees bent at 90 degrees.
Press your lower back flat into the floor.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return to the start and repeat on the other side.
keyCues: Keep your lower back flat against the floor throughout.
Move slowly — this is control, not speed.
Exhale as the limbs extend.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor.
Rushing the reps.
Extending so far the position breaks down.

name: Pallof Press
machineIdentification: A cable pulley set at chest height with a D-handle. You stand side-on and resist the cable's pull to rotate you.
instructions: Set a pulley at chest height with a D-handle.
Stand side-on and hold the handle with both hands at your chest.
Step away until the cable is taut, feet shoulder width.
Press your hands straight out in front of your chest.
Resist the rotation, then bring your hands back in.
keyCues: Don't let the cable twist your torso.
Keep your hips and shoulders square to the front.
Brace hard before each press.
commonMistakes: Letting the torso rotate toward the tower.
Standing too close so there's no resistance.
Pressing with the shoulders instead of bracing the core.

name: Cable Crunch
machineIdentification: A high cable pulley with a rope attached. You kneel facing the tower with the rope beside your head.
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley.
Kneel facing the tower and hold the rope at your temples.
Set your hips back so there's tension at the start.
Curl your ribs down toward your pelvis.
Return under control without letting the stack rest.
keyCues: Round your spine — this is a crunch, not a hinge.
Keep your hips still throughout.
Exhale hard at the bottom of the crunch.
commonMistakes: Hinging at the hips instead of flexing the spine.
Pulling with the arms rather than the abs.
Sitting back onto the heels as the set goes on.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
machineIdentification: A pull-up bar, or a captain's chair — the upright frame with forearm pads and a back rest that lets you hang without gripping.
instructions: Hang from a bar with arms straight, or settle into a captain's chair.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Raise your knees toward your chest, curling your pelvis up.
Lower slowly without swinging.
keyCues: Curl your pelvis at the top — don't just lift the knees.
Keep the swing out of it by pausing at the bottom.
Bend the knees more to make it easier.
commonMistakes: Swinging the body to generate momentum.
Only lifting the legs from the hips with no pelvic curl.
Dropping the legs fast between reps.

name: Farmer's Carry
instructions: Pick up a heavy dumbbell in each hand.
Stand tall with shoulders back and ribs down.
Walk in a straight line with controlled steps.
Reps are counted in seconds of walking.
keyCues: Stand tall — don't let the weight round your shoulders.
Take short, deliberate steps.
Brace your core as if carrying something fragile.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward under the load.
Rushing with long, uncontrolled strides.
Letting the shoulders slump toward the weights.

name: Suitcase Carry
instructions: Pick up a single heavy dumbbell in one hand.
Stand tall with both shoulders level.
Walk in a straight line, resisting the pull to one side.
Switch hands and repeat. Reps are counted in seconds.
keyCues: Keep both shoulders level — don't lean away.
Brace the side opposite the weight.
Walk slowly and deliberately.
commonMistakes: Leaning away from the weight to counterbalance.
Letting the loaded shoulder drop.
Going too light to challenge the core.

name: Overhead Carry
instructions: Press a moderate dumbbell overhead in one hand.
Lock your elbow and keep the weight stacked over your shoulder.
Walk in a straight line, staying tall.
Switch arms and repeat. Reps are counted in seconds.
keyCues: Keep the arm locked and the weight directly overhead.
Tuck your ribs down so the back doesn't arch.
Start much lighter than you expect.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to hold the weight up.
Letting the arm drift forward or out to the side.
Going too heavy and losing the overhead position.
